solutions.check: bars rebuilt from the blog's numbered answers (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Mineral causing variegated rue with pink fleck

indicators.note: something variegated is patched with mixed colours, so the letters are mixed up too

explanation.surface: A mineral that leaves rue plants mottled with pink spots.
explanation.walkthrough: KUPFERNICKEL is the German name for niccolite, a copper-coloured nickel ore.
explanation.definitionFit: Kupfernickel is an old name for the nickel arsenide ore niccolite, so it is a mineral.

clue.text: One aboard turbulent sky-hops in hunched condition

indicators.note: aboard puts one piece inside another as on a ship
turbulent air churns things about

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A passenger on bumpy short flights ends up hunched over.
explanation.definitionFit: Kyphosis is the medical term for excessive outward curvature of the spine, a hunchback.

clue.text: Magpies grabbing end of frill left folded fan-wise

indicators.note: grabbing means holding something inside
end of asks for the final letter of the next word

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: Magpies seize a frilly thing that was left folded like a fan.
explanation.walkthrough: Pica is Latin for magpie and the name of the magpie genus.
explanation.definitionFit: Plical means pleated or folded, like a fan, from the Latin plica, a fold.

clue.text: Coffin I found in Ecuador indicating human settlement

indicators.note: found in puts pieces inside another

parts.note: kist is a Scots word for a chest or coffin

explanation.surface: A coffin discovered in Ecuador points to an ancient settlement.
explanation.definitionFit: Ekistics is the science of human settlements, so ekistic describes something relating to them.

clue.text: Salesman given pay increase or yearly deduction

parts.note: a rep is a sales representative
a rise is an increase in pay

explanation.surface: A salesman offered either a raise or an annual cut in pay.
explanation.walkthrough: A rise is the British term for a pay raise.
explanation.definitionFit: A reprise is a deduction or charge payable annually out of a landed estate's income.

clue.text: Some medic talking about epilepsy?

indicators.note: some means only part of the words that follow is needed

parts.note: letters running across the two words

explanation.surface: A doctor's conversation, possibly on epilepsy.
explanation.definitionFit: Ictal means relating to an ictus, a seizure or stroke, so it describes an epileptic fit; the question mark marks the example.

clue.text: Tea dance? I'll replace second half (same as first)

indicators.note: the latter half of the word gives way to the letter offered

parts.note: the cha-cha is a Latin dance, its two halves identical

explanation.surface: An invitation to a tea dance, with a request for a turn.
explanation.walkthrough: The bracket notes that the second half of the dance name is identical to the first.
explanation.definitionFit: Chai is the Indian word for tea, usually spiced and milky.

clue.text: Locker containing a king's WC

indicators.note: containing means holding the next pieces inside

parts.note: R for rex, king, with the possessive S

explanation.surface: A locker holding the monarch's private lavatory.
explanation.walkthrough: Karsey (also karzy) is British slang for a toilet.
explanation.definitionFit: Karsey is British slang for a lavatory, a WC (water closet).

clue.text: Rakes clearing central area for legumes

definitions.note: Lens is the genus name, standing for the plants collectively

indicators.note: clearing the central part means removing the middle letter

parts.note: to rake is to slope or lean
A is the abbreviation for area

explanation.surface: Garden rakes used to clear a bed for growing beans.
explanation.definitionFit: Lens is the botanical genus of the lentil, so it names a group of legumes.

clue.text: Once cooled down day's not active wandering round mere

indicators.note: round means the shuffled letters go around the outside of the next piece
letters that are wandering drift out of their order
not tells us to leave out the letter for active from the word before

parts.note: A is the grammar abbreviation for active, here removed

explanation.surface: A dawdler cooled off over a day of idle strolling round a lake.
explanation.walkthrough: Once the A is gone, the remaining three letters wrap around the lake. The y- prefix is the old Spenserian past participle marker, as in yclept.
explanation.definitionFit: Yslaked is the old Spenserian participle of slake, meaning quenched or cooled, hence the 'Once' marking it as archaic.

clue.text: Idle ear part's captivated by noise (10, two words)

indicators.note: captivated by means held inside another

parts.note: lobar means of a lobe, the part of the ear

explanation.surface: An idler's earlobe is captivated by a noise.
explanation.definitionFit: To slob around is to laze about doing nothing, to idle.

clue.text: Working apart among vines while dad's still alive (10, two words)

indicators.note: among places the reworked letters inside the next word

parts.note: Vitis is the botanical genus of vines

indicators.note: working suggests something being worked or remade into a new form

explanation.surface: Labouring in the vineyard while father still lives.
explanation.definitionFit: Vita patris is Latin for 'in the father's lifetime', a legal phrase.

clue.text: Swell? Droopy, last to take the lead

indicators.note: the final letter moves up to become the first, rotating the word

explanation.surface: A puzzled reader wonders whether a drooping thing is swollen, with the laggard taking the front.
explanation.walkthrough: PLIM is a dialect word for to swell or fill out.
explanation.definitionFit: In dialect, to plim is to swell or become plump, as in a fattening animal.

clue.text: Sailor in anguish — his views were heretical

indicators.note: in puts the sailor inside the word for anguish

explanation.surface: A sailor in torment whose opinions were judged heretical.
explanation.walkthrough: The Patarins were an eleventh-century Milanese reform movement, and the name was later applied to heretics generally.
explanation.definitionFit: Patarin (or Paterine) was a name for members of a medieval sect regarded by the church as heretics.

clue.text: Cheat that contains nothing? Send it back

indicators.note: sending it back means reading the result from end to start
contains puts the word for nothing inside the word for that

parts.note: such can stand for that, as in 'such is life'

explanation.surface: A con trick revealed as an empty package to be returned.
explanation.walkthrough: O goes into SUCH between C and H, giving SUCOH, which is then reversed.
explanation.definitionFit: To hocus someone is to cheat or trick them, as in hocus-pocus.

clue.text: Jester alternating with fool — they're often belted

indicators.note: the two words are interleaved, each sitting between letters of the other in turn

explanation.surface: A jester and a fool take turns, and one gets belted.
explanation.walkthrough: W-I-T and A-S-S are woven together letter by letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A waist is the middle of the body where a belt is usually worn.

clue.text: Crown of pelican not moving beak at the top?

parts.note: a beak is a headmaster, the person at the top of a school

explanation.surface: A bird's head motionless, its bill held aloft.
explanation.walkthrough: The pelican is not a bird here but a kind of alembic, a still used in distilling; its crown is the stillhead.
explanation.definitionFit: A pelican was a type of distilling vessel, and the stillhead is the upper part or cap of a still.

clue.text: Place for dead flower? A tragedy

definitions.note: the definition includes the article, as 'a disaster'

explanation.surface: A wreath of flowers at the graveyard marks a tragedy.
explanation.definitionFit: A disaster is a sudden calamity, which a tragedy is.

clue.text: Stew of left-overs Islam's thrown out

indicators.note: letters thrown out land in disorder

parts.note: the possessive 's is read as 'is', a link

explanation.surface: Leftover stew that a religion has rejected.
explanation.definitionFit: A salmi is a ragout of game, often made from reheated roasted birds, so a stew from leftovers.

clue.text: Two-up, around second in Masters, showing dominance

indicators.note: around puts the first word outside the selected letter

parts.note: swy is the Australian name for the coin-tossing game two-up, from German zwei

indicators.note: second in asks for the second letter of the following word

parts.note: the second letter of the word

explanation.surface: A golfer two shots ahead in the Masters demonstrates mastery.
explanation.walkthrough: Two-up is an Australian gambling game of tossing two coins, also called swy.
explanation.definitionFit: Sway means power or rule over others, as in 'hold sway'.

clue.text: Being miscast rattles Hollywood wannabe?

indicators.note: being miscast means put in the wrong place

explanation.surface: A would-be film star is unsettled by the wrong part.
explanation.definitionFit: A starlet is a young actress hoping to become a star, a hopeful in films.

clue.text: Rather pale girl in grip of longing

indicators.note: in the grip of means held tightly within

explanation.surface: A lovesick girl turns pale with yearning.
explanation.definitionFit: Wan means pale, and the -ish suffix softens it to somewhat or rather.

clue.text: Paint that's blue or green — or black, introducing formality

indicators.note: introducing means the first piece comes before and leads in the next

parts.note: B is the pencil abbreviation for black
ice is coldness of manner, stiff formality

explanation.surface: Choosing a paint colour: blue, green, or perhaps a formal black.
explanation.definitionFit: Bice is a blue or green pigment made from copper carbonate, used as a paint.

clue.text: Strong wind, a biggy, in storm striking Luxembourg

indicators.note: striking out means crossing a letter off

parts.note: to bluster is to blow or storm
L is the international code for Luxembourg

explanation.surface: A huge gale strikes Luxembourg.
explanation.walkthrough: Two definitions and a wordplay. A buster in Australia is a strong southerly wind; it is also slang for anything unusually large.
explanation.definitionFit: A buster is a violent wind (a southerly buster) and also informally something outstandingly big.

clue.text: See this short prayer I wrung out — in gurdwaras?

indicators.note: wrung out suggests something twisted, so the combined letters get mixed
the answer plus the following letters together make up the final phrase, so taking those away leaves this

parts.note: taken as written, the letters to be removed
taken as written, the full anagram letters

explanation.surface: A short prayer, squeezed out by the speaker, as heard in Sikh temples.
explanation.walkthrough: A composite anagram: the answer plus I WRUNG is an anagram of IN GURDWARAS. A gurdwara is a Sikh temple, where this prayer is recited.
explanation.definitionFit: Ardas is the Sikh set prayer of supplication, said at the end of services in a gurdwara.

clue.text: Do blasting with this? It can make a loud din

indicators.note: can make suggests letters reworked into something new
the first word together with the answer forms the anagram, so it must be taken away again

parts.note: taken as written, the full anagram letters

explanation.surface: Use this for blasting; it makes a racket.
explanation.walkthrough: A composite anagram: DO plus the answer is an anagram of A LOUD DIN.
explanation.definitionFit: Dualin is a dynamite-like explosive of nitroglycerine and sawdust, used for blasting.

clue.text: This is missing in essence, also towards bottom of chart?

indicators.note: in puts what remains inside the word for essence

parts.note: the soul is a thing's essence

indicators.note: is missing tells us the word is should be taken away

explanation.surface: Something lacking at the heart of things, also near the bottom of a table.
explanation.walkthrough: 'This' looks like it refers to the answer, but it is just the word to be trimmed.
explanation.definitionFit: A southland is the southern part of a country, which a map shows at the bottom.

clue.text: Bird? Bird hopes boyfriend will turn this

wordplay.words: Bird hopes boyfriend will turn this
wordplay.note: bird is slang for a girl; what she hopes he will do is a two-word phrase meaning arouse her, with this standing for her

explanation.surface: A girl hoping her boyfriend will excite her.
explanation.walkthrough: Bird is British slang for a girlfriend; the phrase she hopes for is 'turn her on'.
explanation.definitionFit: A heron is a long-legged wading bird.

clue.text: Face Her Majesty like a smart sailor

parts.note: puss is slang for the face

explanation.surface: Confront the Queen, as a smartly turned-out naval rating would.
explanation.definitionFit: Pusser is naval slang meaning formal or correct in a service way, as of a smartly dressed sailor.

clue.text: Doubt lifted, sis having gone off muscles

indicators.note: lifted in a down clue means read from bottom to top
having gone off means removed

explanation.surface: A sister has left, sceptical, flexing her muscles.
explanation.definitionFit: Pecs is the informal word for the pectoral muscles of the chest.

clue.text: Gardens, last coming to the fore in Oxford, say

indicators.note: the final letter moves up to the front

explanation.surface: Oxford college gardens where the last shall be first.
explanation.walkthrough: Oxford looks like the university city, but it is a style of lace-up shoe.
explanation.definitionFit: An Oxford is a lace-up leather shoe, an example of the general word.

clue.text: Approaches calling for attention between bridge partners

indicators.note: between places one piece in the middle of two others

parts.note: North and South are partners at bridge
to give ear is to pay attention

explanation.surface: Bridge players announcing their approach, wanting attention.
explanation.definitionFit: To near something is to approach it, so nears means approaches.

clue.text: Bind in leather, not i.e. for distribution

indicators.note: letters handed out for distribution end up scattered
not tells us to take away the letters that follow

explanation.surface: Bookbinding instructions: cover it in leather, but not in i.e. style.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bind in leather' reads as bookbinding, but the definition is only 'Bind'.
explanation.definitionFit: To enthral originally meant to make a thrall, to enslave or hold in bondage.

clue.text: Slimy stuff from end of slug, legless?

indicators.note: end of asks for the final letter of the next word

parts.note: legless and lit are both slang for drunk

explanation.surface: A slug's slime trail, with the creature wondering if it is legless.
explanation.walkthrough: Legless is British slang for very drunk; slugs have no legs, which drives the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Glit is a dialect word for slime or sticky filth.

clue.text: Scorn, especially when received by side hammered

indicators.note: received by puts one piece inside another
something hammered is beaten out of shape

parts.note: esp. is the abbreviation for especially

explanation.surface: A team that has been thrashed is treated with particular contempt.
explanation.definitionFit: To despise is to look down on with contempt, which is what scorn means as a verb.

clue.text: Booster making gents err wildly, subsequently restrained

indicators.note: restrained means held inside something else
acting wildly means behaving without order

explanation.surface: A stimulant that makes men misbehave, afterwards held back.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that strengthens gives a boost, so a booster is a strengthener.
